title: Panama: a canal climbs
hook: Does a ship simply sail through at sea level?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.
doesNotKnow: Locks lift ships to a lake

objective: Panama is a lock canal, not a sea-level trench.

claims.text: 1914 · 1: Atlantic entrance. A ship approaches the Atlantic locks.
claims.source: https://pancanal.com/en/history-of-the-panama-canal/ — Lock system, Gatun Lake elevation and Atlantic/Pacific locks; https://pancanal.com/en/panama-canal-turns-90/ — August 15, 1914 opening

claims.text: 1914 · 2: Gatun locks. Locks lift the ship toward Gatun Lake.
claims.source: https://pancanal.com/en/history-of-the-panama-canal/ — Lock system, Gatun Lake elevation and Atlantic/Pacific locks; https://pancanal.com/en/panama-canal-turns-90/ — August 15, 1914 opening

claims.text: 1914 · 3: Lake crossing. The ship crosses the elevated lake.
claims.source: https://pancanal.com/en/history-of-the-panama-canal/ — Lock system, Gatun Lake elevation and Atlantic/Pacific locks; https://pancanal.com/en/panama-canal-turns-90/ — August 15, 1914 opening

claims.text: 1914 · 4: Pacific descent. Locks lower the ship toward the Pacific.
claims.source: https://pancanal.com/en/history-of-the-panama-canal/ — Lock system, Gatun Lake elevation and Atlantic/Pacific locks; https://pancanal.com/en/panama-canal-turns-90/ — August 15, 1914 opening

claims.text: Panama is a lock canal, not a sea-level trench. Ships are raised to Gatun Lake, about 26 meters above sea level, and lowered again on the other side. The canal opened in 1914. These steps explain the system rather than reconstructing one named ship’s exact passage.
claims.source: https://pancanal.com/en/history-of-the-panama-canal/ — Lock system, Gatun Lake elevation and Atlantic/Pacific locks; https://pancanal.com/en/panama-canal-turns-90/ — August 15, 1914 opening
